text:
Hi, thanks for getting back to me, and I appreciate you being upfront. £300 is a bit lower than I can go. It was serviced in March and has had new tyres since June, so it's in good shape. I could do £380 if you can collect tonight, which saves us both the hassle of going back and forth.

Let me know if that works and what time you'd like to come by.

Hi, thanks for getting back to me, and sorry to hear you're between jobs. I can't do £300, but I'd be happy to meet you partway at £380. The bike was serviced in March and has new tyres from June, so it's ready to ride. Tonight works for collection if you'd like to come and have a look. Just let me know what time suits you.

Hi, thanks for getting back to me, and I'm sorry to hear you're between jobs. I can't do £300, but I could do £360 if you can collect tonight. It's a 2021 Trek FX 3 Disc in size M, serviced in March with new tyres in June, so it's ready to ride. To be upfront, the gears can be a bit clunky when it's cold and there's a small tear in the saddle, but nothing that affects the ride.

If £360 works for you, come over tonight and have a look. Let me know what time suits.

Hi, thanks for getting back to me, and I appreciate you being upfront about your budget. Unfortunately £5,800 is too low for me. The Octavia has full service history, 82,000 miles and MOT until August, and it's a really solid, well-looked-after car.

I'd like to find a price that works for both of us, though. If you can do £6,500 in cash, I'd be happy to do the deal today and have it ready for you when you arrive. Come and have a look and a drive first, and let me know if that could work.

Thanks,
John

Hi, thanks for getting in touch, and good luck with your studies. I appreciate you being upfront about your budget.

£5,800 is a bit too low for me. The Octavia has full service history and MOT until August, and it's a really solid, well-looked-after estate. I'd be happy to come down to £6,500 for a quick cash sale, which is a good saving on the asking price.

If that's within reach, you're welcome to come and see it, and we can sort it all out on the day. Let me know what you think.

Thanks,
John

Hi, thanks for getting back to me, and good luck with the studies! I can't do £5,800, as it's a 2017 Octavia estate with full service history and MOT until August, and it's priced fairly at £6,900. I'd like it to go to a good home though, and cash on the day makes things simple, so I could do £6,500 if you can stretch to that.

If that works, you're welcome to come and see it and take it for a spin. Just let me know a time that suits you.

Hi Mr Hadley,

Thank you for letting us know, and for being upfront about your costs. We'd very much like to renew for another year. We've been happy in the flat for three years and have paid on time every month.

We understand your costs have gone up, and we're happy to accept an increase. £1,450 is a big jump from the current £1,250, though, and it's more than we can stretch to. We'd like to offer £1,300 a month for a 12-month renewal.

We think that's a fair increase, and you'd be keeping reliable tenants who look after the property and pay on time, with no gaps or hassle for you. If you'd like to talk it through, I'm happy to call or meet.

Best wishes,
John

Hi Mr Hadley,

Thank you for letting us know, and for being upfront about your costs. We'd very much like to renew for another year. We've been happy in the flat and hope to stay on.

Over the three years we've been here, we've paid on time every month, and we'd like to carry on being the kind of tenants who make things easy for you. We understand your costs have gone up, and we're happy to accept an increase. However, £1,450 is a big jump from the current £1,250, and it's more than we can manage.

Would you consider £1,300 a month for a 12-month renewal? That would be a £50 increase, and we'd be glad to sign as soon as we agree on a figure.

Do let me know what you think, and I'm happy to talk it over by phone if that's easier.

Kind regards,
John

Hi Mr Hadley,

Thank you for letting us know, and I understand costs have gone up for you. We'd very much like to renew for another year. We've been happy in the property, and in three years we've never missed or been late with a rent payment.

£1,450 is a big jump from the current £1,250, and more than we can manage. We'd like to propose £1,300 a month for a 12-month renewal. That's an increase of £50 a month, and you'd keep reliable tenants who look after the place and pay on time, with no void period or hassle finding someone new.

If you'd like to talk it through, I'm happy to have a call. Otherwise, let me know if £1,300 works and we can get the paperwork moving.

Best wishes,
John

Hi Marek,

Thanks for coming back to me, and I appreciate the pressure raw material costs have put on everyone this year.

Unfortunately, £2.55 a unit is more than we can work with. We're looking at a firm order of 20,000 units, needed by 1 March, and the unit price has to come down significantly for us to proceed.

Could you take another look at your pricing for that volume and come back with a revised figure? If we can get the price to a workable level, I'm keen to book in with you and get this moving.

Thanks,
John

Hi Marek,

Thanks for coming back to me, and I appreciate raw material costs have been difficult for everyone.

£2.55 a unit is further than we can go. We're looking at a firm order of 20,000 units, needed by 1 March, and I'd like to find a price that works for both of us. Could you do £2.20 a unit? At that price I'm ready to confirm the order.

If you can't reach that, tell me what's the lowest you can do on a 20,000-unit commitment and I'll see what's possible on our side.

Best regards,
John

Hi Marek,

Thanks for coming back to me, and I understand raw material costs have been difficult this year.

Unfortunately, £2.55 a unit is higher than we can make work. We're looking at a firm order of 20,000 units, needed by 1 March, and we'd like to commit to that volume with you. To do so, we'd need the unit price to be closer to £2.20.

Is there any room to get to that level? If it helps, I'm happy to talk about order timing or payment terms to make the numbers work for both of us.

If you can come back with a revised price, I'm keen to get this booked in.

Best regards,
John

Hi,

Thank you, and please pass on my thanks to the team. I really enjoyed meeting them and I'm excited about the role and the work they're doing.

I'm not able to accept at £40,000, as it's well below the advertised £50,000 for the role. I understand budgets are tight, though, and I'd like to find a way to make this work. Would the team be able to move to £48,000? I'm confident I can add real value quickly, and I'd be keen to get started as soon as possible.

If there's flexibility elsewhere in the package, such as a salary review after six months, I'm happy to discuss that too.

Thanks again for your help with this.

Best regards,
John

Hi,

Thank you for passing that on, and please thank the team for me. I'm really enthusiastic about the Product Analyst role and about working with them.

I'm not able to accept at £40,000, as it's well below the advertised £50,000 for the role. I understand budgets are tight, and I'd like to find a way to make this work. Based on the scope of the role and what I'd bring to it, I'd be happy to accept at £47,000.

If there's flexibility in the overall package, such as a salary review after six months, I'm happy to discuss that too.

I'm keen to get started and can join quickly once we agree terms. Could you check with the team and let me know?

Best wishes,
John

Hi,

Thank you, and please pass on my thanks to the team. I'm glad they liked me, and I'm very interested in the role and in working with them.

I can't accept at £40,000, as it's well below the advertised £50,000 and below what I'd expect for the responsibilities involved. I understand budgets are tight. If they can move to £47,000, I'd be happy to accept and can start as soon as they need me.

If the base salary is fixed, I'm open to discussing the overall package, such as a guaranteed salary review after six months, a signing bonus, or extra leave.

Could you take this back to them and let me know what's possible?

Best wishes,

Hi Leo,

Thank you for your message, and I'm sorry to hear about the tax bill. I'm glad Tidewrack III appeals to you. It was shown at Fold Gallery in March, and I think it would suit a home where it gets plenty of light.

I can't agree to £2,600, but I'd like to find something that works. The best I can offer is £3,400, which is a good reduction on the list price of £4,000. If it helps with timing, I'm happy to talk about spreading the payment over a few instalments.

Let me know what you think.

Best wishes,
Studio assistant to Ines

Hi Leo,

Thank you for your message, and I'm sorry to hear about the tax bill. I'm glad Tidewrack III appeals to you, and Ines would love for it to have a good home too.

£2,600 is a little below where we can go, but I can bring the price down from £4,000 to £3,400 for you. If that works, I'll hold the piece for you and send over the details for payment and delivery.

Let me know what you think.

Best wishes,
John
Studio assistant to Ines

Hi Leo,

Thank you for your message, and I'm sorry to hear about the tax bill. I'm glad Tidewrack III appeals to you, and I'd love to see it go to a good home too.

£2,600 is a little lower than Ines can go on this piece, so I can't say yes at that figure. If it helps, I can offer it to you at £3,500 rather than the list price of £4,000. It's a 120 x 90 cm work in oil and beeswax on linen, from 2025, and it was shown at Fold Gallery in March.

If that works for you, let me know and I'll arrange the next steps. If you'd like to see it in person first, I'm happy to set up a studio visit.

Best wishes,
Studio assistant to Ines

Dear Mrs Okoro,

Thank you for your message, and for being so open about the board's budget. I'd be glad to work with the charity.

My standard day rate is £450. For a charity I can offer a reduced rate of £380 a day, which for the 12 days of design work comes to £4,560. That is a significant reduction, and it's as far as I can comfortably go while keeping the quality of work you should expect from me.

If the board's ceiling is firm, I'm happy to look at adjusting the scope instead, such as prioritising the most important pages or screens first and leaving the rest as an optional second phase. That could bring the total closer to your budget without cutting corners on what we do deliver.

I'm experienced in both Figma and Webflow, so I can take the work from design through to a finished build if that would be useful.

Let me know how the board would like to proceed, and I can confirm a start date once we've agreed.

Kind regards,
John

Dear Mrs Okoro,

Thank you for being so open about the board's budget. I'd like to work with you, and I'm glad to support a charity.

£290 a day is below what I can do for this project. My standard day rate is £450, and for a charity I can offer a reduced rate of £400 a day. Over the 12 days, that comes to £4,800 in total, a saving of £600 on my usual rate.

If the board needs a lower figure, I'm happy to look at the scope with you. We could focus on the highest-priority pages or components first, which would reduce the number of days. I'd handle the design in Figma and the build in Webflow, so you'd have one person across the whole project.

Let me know what you think, or if it would help to talk it through, I'm happy to jump on a call.

Kind regards,
John

Dear Mrs Okoro,

Thank you for getting back to me, and for being so open about the board's budget. I'd be glad to work with your charity.

My standard day rate is £450. For the 12 days of design work, I can offer a charity rate of £360 a day, which comes to £4,320 in total. That is a considerable reduction, and it's the lowest I can go while still giving the project the time and care it needs.

If the board can't stretch that far, I'm happy to look at trimming the scope so the work fits a smaller budget. I'd rather agree a focused project that I can do well than rush a larger one.

I'll be using Figma and Webflow, so the design and the build can run together smoothly. If you let me know how the board feels, I can confirm the details and a start date.

Kind regards,
John

Hi,

Thank you for your message, and I'm glad you love the house. It would be lovely to see it go to first-time buyers who appreciate it.

I'm afraid £378,000 is a little below where we can go. The house has a new kitchen fitted in 2023 and a south-facing garden, and we've had good interest at the asking price. That said, I'd like to find a way to make this work for you. If you can come up to £395,000, I'd be happy to agree the sale and get things moving straight away.

Let me know what you think.

Kind regards,
John

Hi,

Thank you for your message. We're glad you love the house, and we'd be happy to find a way to make this work for you.

Unfortunately we can't accept £378,000. It's a fair way below where we need to be, given the new kitchen (2023) and the south-facing garden. We'd be happy to agree a sale at £398,000, and if you can get closer to that figure, we'd be glad to move forward quickly.

If there's any flexibility in your mortgage offer or your budget, let me know and we can see where we land. If you'd like to have another look around the house, I'm happy to arrange that.

Kind regards,
John

Hello,

Thank you for your message, and I'm glad you love the house. It has been a lovely home, and the kitchen was fully redone in 2023 and the south-facing garden gets sun all day.

Unfortunately, £378,000 is lower than we can accept. We're asking £415,000 and have priced it with that in mind. If you can stretch your budget, we'd be happy to consider an offer at £400,000. Is there any room on your side, for example from savings or a larger deposit?

Let me know what's possible and we can take it from there.

Kind regards

Hi Dana,

Thanks for the update. Please hold off on the order form for now.

An increase from £24,000 to £32,500, about 35%, is well beyond what we can take forward. We'd like to renew at our current £24,000 a year for our 85 users, on the existing scope, from 30 June.

If you can, please send:

1. A renewal quote at £24,000 a year for our current plan and user count.
2. A breakdown of what makes up the £32,500, separating the new features from the general cost uplift. If any of the new features are useful to us, we can consider them as optional add-ons rather than part of the base renewal.

We've been happy with Ledgerly and want to continue the relationship, so I'm keen to find something that works for both sides. I'm free for a call this week or next if that would help.

Best regards,
John

Hi Dana,

Thanks for the renewal quote. Please hold off on sending the order form for now.

An increase from £24,000 to £32,500 is a rise of over 35%, which is well beyond what we can take forward. We'd like to renew at our current £24,000 a year for our 85 users.

We understand your costs have gone up, but we haven't asked for the new features and would be happy to renew on our current plan without them. If some of them would be useful to us, we're glad to look at those separately once the base price is settled.

Could you come back with a renewal proposal at £24,000 a year? The contract runs to 30 June, so there's time to get this right, and I'm happy to jump on a call this week or next if that's easier.

Thanks,
John

Hi Dana,

Thanks for the update. Please hold off on the order form at £32,500, as that's a significant jump from what we pay today and isn't something we can take forward.

We'd like to renew at our current rate of £24,000 a year for our 85 users. We've been a steady customer, and we'd like the renewal to reflect that.

If the new features are what's driving the increase, I'd be happy to look at them separately. For the core renewal, though, we need to keep the price flat. Could you send a breakdown of what makes up the £32,500, so we can see which parts are the new features and which are the cost increase?

Once you've had a chance to check what's possible at £24,000, let me know and we can get the paperwork moving well ahead of the 30 June end date.

Thanks,
John

Hi Helen,

Thanks for chasing this with HR, and for the update. I really enjoy the team and want to keep working here.

£60,000 is a step in the right direction, but it's still some way from where I'd hoped to land. This year I led the billing migration, which finished two weeks ahead of schedule, and I'd like my pay to reflect that. Could HR get to £63,000? If they can, I'm happy to accept straight away.

I know you wanted an answer today. Could you take this back to them now and let me know what they say? I'd like to get it settled quickly.

Thanks,
John

Hi Helen,

Thanks for chasing this with HR, I really appreciate it. I'm glad we're closer, but I'm not able to accept £60,000 today.

I love working with this team and want to keep building here. This year I led the billing migration, which finished two weeks early, and I'd like my salary to reflect that contribution. Could HR look again at £63,000? I think that's a fair figure given the scope of what I delivered.

If there's any flexibility on timing, I'd be glad to talk it through tomorrow. I'm happy to jump on a call whenever suits you.

Thanks again for your support on this.

John

Hi Helen,

Thanks for going back to HR and for pushing on this. I appreciate it.

I'm not able to accept £60,000 today, but I do want to get this resolved. I really enjoy working with the team and want to keep doing it.

This year I led the billing migration, which finished two weeks ahead of schedule, and I'd like my pay to reflect that. Could HR look at £62,000? I think that would be fair, and I'd be happy to accept it straight away.

If it would help, I'm glad to talk it through today.

Thanks,
John
